question: Can entanglement defeat repetition as a way to suppress excess wins?
idea: Repeat a finite two-player one-round game independently many times. If the best entangled single-game winning probability is below one, the claim says exceeding that rate by a fixed positive amount becomes exponentially unlikely. Players may coordinate across repetitions using a joint finite-dimensional entangled strategy.
why: Mathematics used to understand physical models, including quantum systems and interacting particles. A theorem concerns a specified model, not every physical situation.

glossary.meaning: The mathematics of uncertainty and random behavior.
A way of measuring the number of independent directions or degrees of freedom; different theories use different notions.

exactClaim: Proves exponential threshold repetition for every finite two-player one-round game: if its entangled value is v < 1, the probability of winning at least a fraction $v+\delta$ of k independent repetitions decays exponentially in k, for $0\lt \delta\lt 1-v$. Arbitrary joint finite-dimensional entangled strategies and correlated question distributions are allowed. )
